correctness.rationale: For x in P_d, Euclidean distance to signed basis vertex equals ||x||_2^2+1-2 sigma x_j. Thus farthest choice selects the opposite sign of a maximal |x_j|. With c=1-lambda>=lambda, any x in the interior and nonzero maximal coordinate m has new |x_j|=c-lambda m and other |x_i|=lambda |x_i|, hence |next_j|-|next_i|>=c-lambda ||x||_1>0. Boundary inputs enter the interior after one step, so at most two initial iterations are needed for permanent selection; u_{n+1}=c-lambda u_n gives a unique alternating limit ±c/(1+lambda)e_j, others decay like lambda^n. No other periodic orbits or fixed points survive. Coordinate permutation symmetry gives Lebesgue basin 1/d. For every lambda>1/2, a perturbation of (1/2,1/2,0,...) has first chosen index switch at next step; this only establishes sharp trapping cutoff, not classification above cutoff. Independent exact rational checks confirmed trapping at lambda=1/2 and switching at lambda=3/4.

originality.rationale: The motivating Abdulaziz farthest-vertex result concerns planar even regular polygons, including planar four-vertex diamonds, not any d>=3 cross-polytope. The published Resultary simplex farthest-vertex contraction theorem treats d+1 equidistant simplex vertices and long cycles, not 2d antipodal vertices. Neither covers exact d antipodal two-cycles, global coordinate trapping, basin volumes and sharp lambda=1/2 threshold in higher dimensions. No dominating general farthest-vertex theorem identified in scoped search.
residual_risks: Unindexed geometric dynamical-systems literature may state an equivalent higher-dimensional antipodal-coordinate contraction theorem.
Tie-resolution affects measure-zero boundary points but not normalized basin-volume result.
The threshold is sharp only for immediate coordinate trapping, not necessarily global attraction for lambda>1/2.
